description:
Racot Palace was built in the second half of the 18th century in the Classicist style. It grew out of a manor of the Bronisz family, which Dorota, a princess by marriage, expanded; after fighting between Russian forces and the Bar Confederates the manor was destroyed, and her son Antoni Barnaba Jabłonowski, voivode of Poznań, enlarged the manor into a palace and laid out an English-style park behind it. The design is most often attributed to Dominik Merlini, though that is uncertain. Józef Wybicki, who lived in the region, wrote plays for the local theatre, and Tadeusz Kościuszko and Prince Józef Poniatowski are among the recorded visitors.

In 1799 the estate was sold to William I of Orange, later king of the Netherlands; in the late 19th century it passed as a dowry to the princely family of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, and Grand Duke William Ernest added the north wing in 1902.

After the Treaty of Versailles the estate passed to the Polish state, and in 1921 the Council of Ministers designated the palace a residence for the presidents of the Republic of Poland. The palace was renovated in 1968–1970 and again in 2000–2004, after which a training and recreation centre was established there. It is a protected monument, registered in 1952, and today operates as a three-star hotel with free parking, free Wi-Fi and breakfast included on the rate seen.

faqs.question: Who built Racot Palace?
faqs.answer: It was built in the second half of the 18th century in the Classicist style, when Prince Antoni Barnaba Jabłonowski enlarged an earlier manor into a palace; the design is most often attributed to Dominik Merlini, though the attribution is uncertain.

faqs.question: Did Polish presidents stay at Racot Palace?
faqs.answer: In 1921 the Council of Ministers designated the palace as a residence for the presidents of the Republic of Poland, and President Ignacy Mościcki spent a two-week holiday there in July 1927.

Free cancellation applied before 21 November on the rate seen, with no prepayment and payment at the property.

**On-site:** On-site parking and free Wi-Fi.
